messages:
julia-acme: hey @olivia — we're seeing occasional high latency and the console is showing our region as eu-north, but our traces show requests served from us-central. started ~2026-03-15 10:02 UTC. sample request id: req-20260315-5b9f
ops-bot: AUTOMATED: routing-failover detected for req-20260315-5b9f — fallback performed to us-central (reason: capacity-pressure eu-north)
olivia-support: thanks — can you paste the full response headers (curl) and the trace id?
julia-acme: here's a quick curl we captured: ```curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "x-region-prefer: eu-north" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'``` response headers included: `x-serving-region: us-central`, `x-routing-reason: fallback_capacity`, `x-request-id: req-20260315-5b9f`
kevin-sre: we observed a short capacity spike in eu-north and triggered cross-pop failover at 2026-03-15T10:01:58Z. the control plane should surface served-region in the request detail view — can you screenshot the console panel you're looking at?
julia-acme: console shows just "Region: eu-north (primary)" on the request detail. no explicit served-from or serving-region badge. billing UI also lists the request under eu-north usage which is confusing. extra ~120ms tail latency when it hits us-central.
sanjay-runtime: quick check — are you on token-scoped routing / org pinning? pinning can change how the console labels region vs actual serve. Need trace id to confirm path.
julia-acme: trace id is trace-0a1b2c3d. attaching HAR and a small curl log.
kevin-sre: pulled the trace — confirmed the request proxied to us-central with header `x-routing-reason=fallback_capacity` and `x-serving-region=us-central`. runtime emitted fallback and runtime metrics show eu-north at 94% capacity for that interval. UI pipeline that populates the console region label pulls config (primary region) not last-served region in realtime — looks like a race/UX gap.
olivia-support: sorry for the confusion — I'll open an internal ticket and escalate to eng-runtime (P2) and finance for the billing mismatch. we can provisionally credit cross-pop charges if validated.
sanjay-runtime: note for ENG: short-term patch is to expose `served_from` in the request metadata and prefer it for console display. longer-term: sync the telemetry path so billing and console use the same serviced-events stream. filing INF-2247.
kevin-sre: workaround for now: you can verify serving pop via the raw headers endpoint: `GET /v1/requests/{id}/raw-headers` (requires support token). i'll DM steps.
julia-acme: thanks — that helps a lot. we'll pull the raw-headers and follow up if we see more. :thumbsup:
olivia-support: thanks everyone — assigning to @sanjay-runtime and tagging for next-week fix. will keep Julia updated.
